newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-KNOX CELEBRATES RECALL TO WALLABY TEAM.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-KNOX CELEBRATES RECALL TO WALLABY TEAM.

text.p: Australian rugby union fly-half David Knox will put his South African sojourn on hold after making a triumphant return to the international arena on Saturday.

Knox, 33, kicked three penalties and two conversions as Australia beat South Africa 32-20 in the Tri-Nations series in Brisbane, just a month after he left Australia to play provincial rugby in South Africa after being convinced his test career was over.
He had been in outstanding form with the ACT Brumbies during the Super-12 series, but selectors ignored his credentials and gambled instead by switching veteran centre Tim Horan to fly-half.
So Knox applied and was granted permission by the Australian Rugby Union to accept a deal with Natal under the proviso that he return to play for his country if needed.
The recall clause was put into action last week after Horan, whose performances in the No. 10 jersey had been roundly criticised, fractured his hand in last weekend's loss to New Zealand.
Knox was summoned home to join the Australian team for their next game, ironically, against South Africa.
The evergreen fly-half arrived just four days before the match, but slotted in easily and was one of Australia's best playersd in their convincing win.
Knox's initial disappointment at missing out on the Australian team had been countered in part by how much he had enjoyed playing with Natal.

He has already pledged to return to Natal this season but his performance against some of his new teammates on Saturday ensured he will retain his place in the Australian team for the upcoming Tri-Nations tests in New Zealand and South Africa.
Knox played down his performance on Saturday.
"I was just happy to be back. I'm part of a team and I'm happy if I've played all right and the backline has gone well," he said.
Australia scored four tries to three with man-of-the-match Ben Tune crossing for two, in the 19th and 40th minutes.
Number eight Daniel Manu and full back Stephen Larkham grabbed Australia's other touchdowns while prop Os du Randt, fly-half Jannie De Beer and lock Mark Andrews scored for the Springboks.
